title: A Supabase service_role or secret key in browser code lets anyone skip every RLS policy
symptoms: The service_role key or an sb_secret_ key is set in a NEXT_PUBLIC_ variable or passed to createClient in a client component
The key can be found in the JavaScript your site sends to visitors
Requests made with a new secret key from the browser fail with HTTP 401 Unauthorized
cause: Secret keys and the legacy service_role key act as the service_role role, which has the BYPASSRLS attribute, so a request made with one ignores every Row Level Security policy. Supabase blocks new secret keys in browsers by User-Agent, but anyone who copies a key out of a web page, a shipped app or source control can still use it outside a browser.
fix: Use only the publishable key (or the legacy anon key) in browser and mobile code, and keep secret keys in server-only environment variables without the NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix. If a secret key was ever shipped or committed, fix the cause of the leak first, then create a new secret key, replace it everywhere, confirm every component uses it, and delete the old one.
affected: Supabase projects using a secret key or the legacy service_role key; Supabase is deprecating the anon and service_role keys by the end of 2026
